name: oha
what_it_is: oha is a Rust-based HTTP load generator inspired by rakyll/hey that sends configurable bursts of requests to a target URL. It features a real-time terminal UI (TUI) built with ratatui and an async runtime powered by tokio.
components: CLI binary (oha) — single executable, no daemon
Real-time TUI — ratatui-based live dashboard (disable with --no-tui)
Async HTTP engine — tokio runtime with keep-alive connection pooling
SQLite sink — optional per-request result storage via --db-url
JSON output schema — machine-readable results defined in schema.json
protocols: HTTPS via rustls (default) or native-tls (optional feature)
HTTP/HTTPS through proxy (--proxy, supports HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2 to proxy)
measurement: Requests per second (mean, stddev, min, max, percentiles p10–p99.99)
Total body data transferred (bytes), size per request, size per second
configuration: -n <N_REQUESTS>: total requests to send (default 200; supports k/m suffixes)
-z <DURATION>: time-bounded run instead of fixed request count (e.g. 10s, 3m)
-q <QPS>: global rate limit in queries per second
--burst-delay / --burst-rate: send N requests every D seconds
--latency-correction: corrected latency to avoid coordinated omission (requires -q)
--rand-regex-url: generate random URLs per request using regex syntax
--urls-from-file: read target URLs from a newline-delimited file
-d / -D / -Z / -F: request body from string, file, file-per-line, or multipart form
--no-tui: disable live dashboard for higher throughput
--debug: single request with full request/response dump
--ipv4 / --ipv6: restrict DNS resolution to one address family
fault_injection: No built-in fault injection; oha is a client-side load generator only
Errors are recorded and reported (errorDistribution field in JSON output)
Requests aborted at deadline are counted separately from errors
modes: TUI mode (default): real-time dashboard with live latency histograms and status codes
No-TUI mode (--no-tui): headless, higher throughput, avoids per-request data aggregation overhead
Fixed-count mode (-n): run until N requests are completed
Duration mode (-z): run for a fixed wall-clock duration
Rate-limited mode (-q): cap throughput at a global QPS ceiling
Burst mode (--burst-delay + --burst-rate): send N requests every D seconds
Debug mode (--debug): single request with full request/response dump
Docker mode: official image ghcr.io/hatoo/oha, run with --network=host
constraints: HTTP/3 support is experimental and only works with rustls TLS backend
Redirect following is not supported for HTTP/2
Dynamic scheme/host/port in --rand-regex-url do not work well with keep-alive
--latency-correction is silently ignored when -q is not set
--burst-delay and --burst-rate are ignored when -q (QPS) is specified
On HTTP/1 with -z, ongoing requests are aborted at deadline (use -w to wait); on HTTP/2 ongoing requests are always waited and -w is ignored
-p (HTTP/2 parallel streams) multiplies total concurrency: total workers = c * p
Connection limit (-c) may require raising OS open-file limits for large values
Unix socket (--unix-socket) only works with non-HTTPS URLs
docker_services: ghcr.io/hatoo/oha — official pre-built image (multi-arch); ENTRYPOINT is /bin/oha, pass arguments directly; use --network=host to reach services on the host
notable_absences: No docker-compose file in the repository — oha ships only a single-stage Dockerfile
No built-in server or target service — oha requires an external HTTP target
No scripting or scenario DSL (unlike k6 or Gatling)
No persistent configuration file — all options via CLI flags only
